## Example 6.6 {#ss6-example-6-6 .gs-lesson .gs-sigma-example}

Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{k=2}^{10}3^k$.

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 39 · Example 6.6</p>

::: notes


The first included term is a=3²=9, r=3, and n=10−2+1=9. Sum=9(3^9−1)/(3−1)=88569. A useful independent check is (3^11−1)/2−1−3=88569. Count terms before substituting into the sum formula. The k in the summation is a dummy index; n in the sum formula is the number of included terms.

:::
